facts.value: An unhealthy diet is a major risk factor for a number of chronic diseases including high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, abnormal blood lipids, overweight/obesity, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer.

facts.value: Estimates indicate that non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease are responsible for 41 million deaths each year, almost two-thirds of all deaths globally.

facts.value: The World Health Organization has estimated that 2.7 million deaths each year are attributable to a diet low in fruit and vegetables during the 21st century.

facts.value: At least 1.2 billion women are low of vitamins and minerals, which increases the risk of being exposed to chronic fatigue, low resistance to infections, and birth defects in their offspring.

facts.value: Globally, unhealthy diets are estimated to cause about 19% of gastrointestinal cancer, 31% of ischemic heart disease, and 11% of strokes, making it one of the leading preventable causes of death worldwide.

facts.value: Unhealthy diets are the 4th leading risk factor for any disease.
